source_evidence: Exact player 'Well by your own lady’s claim… I actually think it does settle ownership' challenges consistency of Caul's asserted ancient-charter authority after actual documentary comparison. Voss reluctantly acknowledges that if ancient charters remain binding their originating Vaishnavi authority cannot be selectively disregarded, and if invalid their collections lack that asserted justification. His acknowledgment is the conditional logical consequence of his employer's argument, not a verified adjudication of V's genealogy, modern ownership, superior legal title or automatic transfer of authority. Cirren agrees with the argument. Voss states his delegated authority is administration, not surrendering the tower, offers to arrange a direct meeting with Lady Caul; no invitation sent, appointment agreed, messenger dispatched, response from Caul or handover. No actual cessation of collections or additional documentary inspection. Voss remains willing to discuss immediate relief for residents separately. No contested order/concession adjudicated, ordinary dialogue, no roll, combat, spending or resource use. Time D333~16:02. V chooses response.
